findings_qualitative.value: Substituting 12C with 13C in 2-hydroxyacetonitrile has very limited influence on the tunneling Hamiltonian parameters, whereas deuteration of the hydroxyl group (DOCH2CN) strongly alters the tunneling splitting E.

evidence.quote: From the analysis of Table 1, it can be clearly seen that 12 C to 13 C isotopic substitution has a very limited influence on tunneling Hamiltonian parameters.
The deuteration of the hydroxyl group hydrogen implies a significant variation of the mass of the tunneling atom which has a direct influence on the tunneling probability

findings_qualitative.value: None of the three isotopologues (HO13CH2CN, HOCH213CN, DOCH2CN) are detected in existing ALMA observations towards Serpens SMM1-a or IRAS16293 B.

evidence.quote: Only non-detections could be reported in this work toward SMM1-a and IRAS16293 B with no significant constraints on the 13 C/ 12 C and D/H ratios of this molecule.

findings_qualitative.value: Serpens SMM1-a is a better candidate target than IRAS16293 B for future follow-up ALMA observations targeting the strongest transitions of 2-hydroxyacetonitrile isotopologues.

evidence.quote: Given the lower constraints obtained for IRAS16293 B and the small spectral range covered by the observations of SMM1-a so far, it appears that SMM1-a would be a better target for follow-up observations.

claims.hypothesis: The rotational spectra of the 2-hydroxyacetonitrile isotopologues HO13CH2CN, HOCH213CN, and DOCH2CN between 150 and 530 GHz can be accurately modeled using the Reduced Axis System (RAS) formalism.
claims.experiment: Synthesized the three isotopologues, measured their rotational spectra from 150 to 530 GHz with the Lille spectrometer, and fitted over 3000 transitions per species using SPFIT.
claims.result: Fitted 3403 lines for HO13CH2CN (rms 26.3 kHz), 3235 lines for HOCH213CN (rms 28.7 kHz), and 3190 lines for DOCH2CN (rms 26.6 kHz), in good agreement with ab initio rotational constants.
claims.finding: Accurate line lists up to 600 GHz and partition functions were successfully produced for all three isotopologues.

evidence.quote: More than 3000 lines were fitted for the three studied isotopologues, with quantum number values reaching 60 to 67 for J and 21 to 25 for K a depending on the species.
Accurate line lists up to 600 GHz and partition functions are provided.

claims.hypothesis: The 13C and deuterated isotopologues of 2-hydroxyacetonitrile can be detected in ALMA spectra of Serpens SMM1-a and IRAS16293 B where the main isotopologue is known to exist.
claims.experiment: Searched for rotational transitions of HO13CH2CN, HOCH213CN, and DOCH2CN in ALMA Band 6 observations of SMM1-a and in the ALMA-PILS survey and archival cubes of IRAS16293 B using CASSIS and ATOMIS.
claims.result: No transitions were detected above the noise or unblended; upper limits on column densities resulted in 13C/12C ≤ 0.27 and D/H ≤ 0.14 in SMM1-a, and 13C/12C ≤ 0.5 and D/H ≤ 0.5 in IRAS16293 B.
claims.finding: The isotopologues are undetected in current ALMA datasets, providing no strong constraints on isotopic ratios, largely because the SMM1-a spectral windows missed the strongest transitions.

evidence.quote: This results in [isotopologue]/[HOCH 2 CN] ratios of ≤ 0.14 and ≤ 0.27 for the deuterated and 13 C hydroxyacetonitrile isotopologues, respectively.
Only non-detections could be reported in this work toward SMM1-a and IRAS16293 B with no significant constraints on the 13 C/ 12 C and D/H ratios of this molecule.

why_this_data.value: Serpens SMM1-a and IRAS16293 B are the only two astronomical sources where the main isotopologue of 2-hydroxyacetonitrile has been detected so far.

evidence.quote: Later, a second detection of hydroxyacetonitrile was reported towards Serpens SMM1-a (Ligterink et al. 2021). These two detections are thus far the only observations of this molecule.

The main isotopologue of hydroxyacetonitrile has been detected towards Serpens SMM1-a (hereafter SMM1-a) at high abundance (Ligterink et al. 2021), making this a suitable target to search for its isotopologues DOCH 2 CN, HO 13 CH 2 CN and HOCH 13 2 [CN.

why_this_method.value: The Reduced Axis System (RAS) approach in SPFIT/SPCAT is particularly suitable for molecules exhibiting double-minimum large amplitude motion due to OH-group torsion.

evidence.quote: This method is particulary suitable for double minimum LAM cases, we employed it successfully in previous studies (Motiyenko et al. 2010; Smirnov et al. 2013; Motiyenko et al. 2015) and in particular with the hydroxyacetonitrile normal species (Margulès et al. 2017).

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Analyzing the trans rotamer of hydroxyacetonitrile, which was omitted because it lies 1.41 kcal mol^-1 (710 K) higher in energy than the gauche rotamer.

evidence.quote: As for the parent isotopic species, we only analyzed the spectra of the gauche rotamer, which is the most stable one. The trans rotamer of hydroxyacetonitrile is calculated to be 1.41 kcal.mol −1 (493 cm −1 /710 K) higher in energy (Dalbouha et al. 2017).

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Using the parent or 13C tunneling and Coriolis parameters as starting values for DOCH2CN, which was rejected because deuteration of the hydroxyl group strongly alters the tunneling dynamics.

evidence.quote: Therefore, for DOCH 2 CN isotopic species, as starting set of tunneling and Coriolis coupling parameters, we could not use the ones determined for the parent or 13 C species.

limitations_admitted.value: The 1.2" synthetic beam in the SMM1-a observations is insufficient to resolve the hot corino.

evidence.quote: A synthetic beam of approximately 1.2” was employed, which is insufficient to resolve the hot corino.

limitations_admitted.value: The spectral windows of the SMM1-a observations miss most of the strongest transitions of the three isotopologues.
